1.why: The /api/verify handler compares the submitted code or token with the value stored in the current session, but it does not independently prove ownership of the supplied account identifier.

2.why: Each recovery code or token is stored only in the session that requested it, so a code from one session will not verify in another session.

3.why: Changing a password updates the account hash and current session only, while other unexpired session entries are not revoked.

4.why: Bun.serve is started with TLS certificates and HTTP via x-forwarded-proto is rejected, but no minimum or latest TLS version is explicitly configured or observable.

5.why: Reset codes and identifiers are kept as plaintext values in server-side session state, although passwords are bcrypt hashed and TLS protects transport.

6.why: The recovery delivery is simulated by returning and logging the manual code and verification URL, so the message does not hide the secret recovery data.

7.why: User inputs are constrained by validation regexes and length checks, and client-side dynamic output uses textContent instead of innerHTML.

8.why: The only verification link is a same-origin /verify path or hardcoded localhost URL, and no open redirect or external redirect target is present.

9.why: There are no email templates in the code, and the simulated delivery messages are plain text rendered without user-supplied HTML or scripts.

10.why: The visible Logs panel and console.log output expose the manual recovery code and MFA code, even though error pages are generic.

11.why: A static MFA code and an initial bcrypt hash are embedded in the source, so secret material is present in code.

12.why: The fixed MFA code 246810 is hardcoded and accepted, which is a default credential.

13.why: The fail and allowed functions impose progressive 429 delays after repeated failed recovery, verify, MFA, password, and login attempts.

14.why: Unknown identifiers are sent to a sink account and generic messages are returned, avoiding disclosure of whether an identifier exists.

15.why: Recovery codes are generated with crypto.getRandomValues as high-entropy base64url strings and stored per session/account request, though identifier ownership is not separately verified.
